questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses offered by the host university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: none. they had sent some directions from the airport to the dorms

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Only dorms. Single or double room was assigned randomly

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is cheap and nice to live close to other exchange students. However, a challenge knowing that single rooms are assigned randomly.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It is very competetive and stressful. Dorm wifi might crash so i recomend going elsewhere with an internet connection for course registration. 

You log in to the platform and type in Course number and class number. Class number is important to make sure the class is taught in english. The platform does not allow you to sign up for classes that conflict in schedule.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You log in to the platform when application period starts. You fill out the form and supply the documents needed. I got an acceptance email 2 days after i had sent my application.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: None really. KU kinda helped.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: i got 4/5 classes that I wanted and had to end up taking a class i didnt want. There is a course add and drop period the first week where you are able to change course selection.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: don't worry too much but be smart. (e.g. sign up early, go to an internet cafe, ...)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of my courses were easy since they were offered in eglish. For local students english is a challenge meaning that the courses offered in english are somewhat on an academically easier level bc the language in and ofitself is a challenge

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Different. There are quizzes and assignments scattered throughtout the semester as well as midterms and finals. These however are only a 1-2 hour in person exam, sometimes written by hand.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
international Leadership and society 
Critical thinking and moral theories 
understanding north korean politics 
us minority literaure 
introduction to counseling

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: us minority literature is really interesting, with god books and online giving you freedom.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: the first week you spend a lot of money at daiso just to get things you need for the dorm that is not included: towels, soap, storage, and other things.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most things were less expensive than i thought. food is inexpenisve, meaning you can eat comfortably for 100 kr a day (cafe breakfast and restaurant dinner)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: joining clubs is not possible but ewha offers field trips and other events

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
EWHAInMe a christian club for international students, 
EKLES where they pair you up with a korean student
PEACE BUDDY where they pair you up with a korean student

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Peace buddy definetly!!!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: spend the weekends exploring the seoul thats a bit further away and spend the weekdays exploring the seoul neighbourhoods closeby through cafes and restaurants

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easier than i thought

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: sign up for peace buddy

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none. I was prepared for a certain exoticism as well as discrimination. Neither is as bad as feared

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The curiousity

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. i recommend living on dorms 2. i recomend saving up so you can do fun activities 3. do not stress about the academic level of the courses

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: check out the @ucphabroad posts on EWHA

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: realising that it was easier than i had thought

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: looking forward to it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
